subject: Chemistry
question: Use the standard enthalpies of formation in the supplied table to calculate the standard enthalpy change of combustion of ethanol: C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l).

supplied_texts.title: Standard enthalpies of formation at 298 K (extract)
supplied_texts.text:
Substance / ΔH_f° (kJ mol⁻¹)
C₂H₅OH(l) −277
CO₂(g) −394
H₂O(l) −286
O₂(g) 0
supplied_texts.provenance: data table supplied with the question

response_text:
C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l)

ΔH° = ΣΔH_f(products) − ΣΔH_f(reactants)
ΔH° = [2(−394) + 3(−286)] − [(−277) + 3(0)]
= (−788 − 858) − (−277)
= −1646 + 277
= −1369 kJ mol⁻¹

The O₂ term is zero because oxygen is an element in its standard state.
